instructor:
First, a note about the instructor himself. Özgür hoca is great at teaching you the concepts and methods you use to analyze foreign policy. He knows how to engage his students too, so I hardly ever felt bored in his classes. One issue I have is that he doesn't seem to want to spend much time talking with his students outside of class hours, although when he does he is quite nice. I think he must be very busy, but what fault do we students have in this citation-oriented, publish-or-perish academic atmosphere?

On the down side, I think his exams rely too much on simple repetition of the concepts you see during the class. Honestly, I cannot make sense of his exams. They are not memorization-oriented as they were both open-book, but when you do sometimes simply write down what is on the articles or your notes, you might still struggle to get good grades. What I mean is, after taking two classes from him, I still do not know how he grades his exams. I think he really should revise his exams to involve more independent thinking and maybe even some outside knowledge. That would make the exams more intellectually satisfying.
